Claude Code vs Codex: how many tokens they use before and during work

Before doing anything, Claude Code sends 35,776 input tokens and Codex 14,748. On the same browser-game task Codex used 40% fewer input tokens and 47% fewer output tokens than Claude Code. Adding 30 MCP tools barely changed either.

Measured 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-22 · Claude Code 2.1.295 and Codex CLI 0.162 · 4 startup and 5 task runs per tool · License CC BY 4.0 · Related: Claude effort levels

DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23448342 · Also on Hugging Face · Kaggle · GitHub

Key findings

  • Claude Code starts 143% heavier. A one-word reply costs 35,776 input tokens in Claude Code and 14,748 in Codex. That fixed amount is sent again with every request, so it adds up over a session even though most of it is cached.
  • Adding MCP tools barely changed startup tokens. The full definitions of our 30 test tools are 4,541 tokens, but adding them raised Claude Code by only 391 tokens (about 13 per tool) and Codex by nothing measurable. Both now load a tool’s details only when it is needed.
  • Using the tools is what costs. Asked to list the 10 tracker tools and call one, Codex used 47,876 input tokens, 225% more than its plain startup.
  • Same task, about half the tokens on Codex. The browser game took Claude Code 87,779 input and 7,669 output tokens on average (62 s, $0.39 at API prices) and Codex 52,762 input and 4,073 output tokens (56 s). All 10 games worked.
  • Claude Code wrote more code. Its games averaged 474 lines against 58 for Codex, which wrote denser code with fewer line breaks; both had every requested feature.

Method

  • Both tools on the same Windows laptop, each run in its own empty folder.
  • Claude Code 2.1.295 with its default model (Opus 5.5) on a Max plan: claude -p --output-format json, MCP servers only from --mcp-config with --strict-mcp-config; the task at --effort medium with --permission-mode acceptEdits. Input tokens are input + cache creation + cache read; the cost is Claude Code’s own API-price figure.
  • Codex CLI 0.162 with its default model (gpt-6-luna) on a ChatGPT plan: codex exec --json, reasoning effort low for the startup test and medium for the task; the MCP server added with -c mcp_servers.…. Input tokens include cached tokens. No price is shown because Codex reports none on a ChatGPT plan.
  • MCP test server: a small stdio server we wrote that exposes 1, 10 or 30 tracker tools (create, update, list issue and so on), each with a one-sentence description and a five-field input schema.
  • Each finished game was opened in a headless browser: no errors, and two levels, a score and three lives on screen.

Limitations

  • Four startup runs and five task runs per tool, on two days with the same versions, and one task. Claude Code’s task runs ranged from 77,868 to 123,666 input tokens, Codex’s from 47,954 to 70,704.
  • Default models differ (Opus 5.5 vs gpt-6-luna), and the price per token differs too, so fewer tokens does not automatically mean cheaper.
  • Startup tokens include each tool’s installed skills and plugins on this machine; a fresh install may start lower.
  • Cursor will be added when its free-plan limit resets.
